title: Ulyana and the Parish
premise: Ulyana Yarrow, a reclusive estate lawyer in the fog-bound parish of Hollowmere, is summoned to read the will of Edric Vale—a will no court has record of, naming a beneficiary who died years ago. Before the reading concludes, a stranger's body is discovered on the parish steps, dressed head to toe in clothing stolen from Ulyana's own closet, a message meant for her alone. As she is pulled into an investigation she never wanted, Ulyana realizes the killer is someone who has studied the old Vale case file with obsessive intimacy—someone tied to the wrongful conviction that destroyed a family a decade ago. Racing the killer's escalating taunts, Ulyana forms an unlikely found family among the parish's outcasts and risks her career and heart on a disgraced constable, before finally luring the murderer into a trap of her own design and exposing the parish elders who buried the original crime.
about_author: Orsen Thackeray is the pen name of a former parish clerk who spent eleven years transcribing coroner's inquests in rural England before turning to fiction. Their debut draws on the quiet cruelties of small communities, where justice is often a matter of who keeps the records.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't Filed
chapters.summary: Ulyana Yarrow, POV. Summoned on a rain-slicked evening to Hollowmere parish house, Ulyana is handed Edric Vale's will—unregistered, undated, and naming a beneficiary dead for ten years. Her professional instincts scream forgery; her loneliness whispers that she's finally been chosen for something. Beat: uneasy curiosity, the first crack in her careful invisibility.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Before the reading concludes, the verger finds a stranger dead on the parish steps, dressed in garments stolen from Ulyana's own wardrobe—down to a monogrammed scarf. The constable's questions turn toward her. Beat: violation and fear; the watcher has become the watched.

chapters.title: The Constable Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV; brief interlude in Inspector Dane's. Disgraced ex-constable Rowan Pike, once Ulyana's law-school friend, returns unofficially to consult. Their charged reunion is interrupted by Dane's hostility. Beat: reluctant alliance, old affection rekindled against both their judgments.

chapters.title: What the Vale Family Buried
chapters.summary: Rowan, POV. Rowan digs into the decade-old case: Edric Vale's son hanged himself in prison for a murder Rowan never believed he committed. The dead stranger's fingerprints match no records—yet his shoes contain Hollowmere churchyard soil. Beat: dawning horror that the parish itself is complicit.

chapters.title: The Widow's Second Grief
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana interviews Maren Vale, the convicted man's mother, who receives her with terrifying calm: 'I wondered when you'd come.' Maren reveals the will is genuine—she wrote it, and she knows who the stranger was. Beat: grief weaponized into patience.

chapters.title: Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: Rowan, POV. Forensics show the victim was killed elsewhere, dressed post-mortem, and posed with surgical knowledge of the original crime scene photographs—photographs sealed by the court. Someone inside the system leaked them. Beat: the enemy is institutional, not just personal.

chapters.title: Parish Records and Small Lies
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana cross-examines the parish council's minutes and finds pages razored out around the murder date. Elder Cornelius Ashe watches her with polite menace and offers her a quiet bribe to close the estate. Beat: temptation and defiance; she refuses for the first time in her careful life.

chapters.title: The Outcasts' Table
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Sheltering from Ashe's surveillance, Ulyana falls in with the parish's overlooked: Maren, the verger Tamsin, and a runaway kitchen boy, Pip. Over bad stew, they form an accidental investigative household. Beat: warmth; found family taking root in suspicion's shadow.

chapters.title: A Second Message, Folded Neatly
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. A letter arrives in Ulyana's own handwriting—forged flawlessly—inviting her to the old Vale mill at midnight. She goes with Rowan hidden nearby and finds only a chair, a noose, and the original case file, annotated in red. Beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Annotator's Hand
chapters.summary: Rowan, POV. The file's marginalia correct the official record with intimate detail—only someone present at the original scene, or the investigator himself, could know it. Rowan suspects his old mentor, retired Inspector Halloway. Beat: betrayal of a father figure.

chapters.title: Dane Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Inspector Dane, pressured by the council, charges Ulyana with obstruction and seizes the estate's documents. Her license hangs by a thread; clients scatter. Beat: despair at its lowest ebb; duty weaponized against justice.

chapters.title: Pip Sees Something
chapters.summary: Pip, POV (first child's-eye chapter). The kitchen boy, running an errand for Ashe, glimpses a figure in the vestry burning papers—and recognizes the dead stranger's distinctive limp on a man very much alive. Beat: innocence carrying dangerous knowledge.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Hanged
chapters.summary: Rowan, POV. The revelation lands: the stranger wore the face and gait of Daniel Vale—the convicted man whose body was never independently identified. Either he didn't die in prison, or someone has been wearing his life. Beat: vertigo; the past refuses its grave.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession, Partly True
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Maren admits she smuggled her son out of prison with Halloway's help, faking his death—but swears Daniel returned changed, hollow, and vanished again two years ago. The will was her beacon to draw the truth home. Beat: love against duty, a mother's crime forgiven.

chapters.title: Halloway's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Rowan, POV. Rowan confronts Halloway at his cottage and finds him dying of a stroke, clutching a ledger proving the original murder was committed by Cornelius Ashe—and covered up by the parish council to protect their land dealings. Beat: the mentor's silence as final gift and curse.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Vestry
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. The vestry burns overnight; the parish records are destroyed, and Tamsin the verger is found unconscious, having tried to save them. Ulyana realizes the killer isn't Daniel—it's someone protecting Ashe, someone inside her own circle of trust. Beat: heartbreak and recalibration.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Reading Room
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana announces a public second reading of the will, seeding it with a false clause that only the killer would find significant. She, Rowan, Maren, and Pip stage the parish house like a stage set. Beat: agency reclaimed; the invisible woman becomes the lure.

chapters.title: The Verger's Vigil
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Tamsin, waking and cornered, confesses: she was Daniel's secret wife, and when he returned broken and threatened to expose Ashe, she killed him—then dressed the body in Ulyana's clothes to make the lawyer, the one person Daniel trusted, carry the guilt she couldn't bear. Beat: love curdled into murder.

chapters.title: Night at the Second Reading
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. The trap springs: Tamsin, hearing the false clause name her as beneficiary, breaks—and Ashe, arriving to silence the reading, is caught by Rowan and Dane, whose loyalty finally turns when the ledger surfaces. Beat: climax; every debt called in under one roof.

chapters.title: What the Court Cannot Touch
chapters.summary: Rowan, POV. Ashe's lawyers descend, but the outcasts' evidence—Pip's testimony, Halloway's ledger, Maren's sworn statement—forces an inquest. Rowan chooses to testify about his own old failures, trading his reputation for the truth. Beat: justice outside the law, purchased with sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Reading at Last
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. The will is finally read aloud in the repaired parish house: the estate goes to Maren, with a trust for Pip's schooling, and a letter from Daniel forgiving his mother. Ulyana, publicly cleared, declines to restore her old practice. Beat: grief transmuted into legacy.

chapters.title: Ulyana and the Parish
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Months later, Ulyana keeps a small office above the parish house, counsel to those the system overlooks, with Rowan's coat on her hook and Sunday stew at Maren's table. A new client knocks with an impossible case, and this time Ulyana opens the door smiling. Beat: belonging earned; the invisible woman found.
